comment_data.body:
@Kogaraashi1  The issue occurs because when trying to delete a buffer with `<C-d>`, the list of buffers isn't updated as expected. This happens due to how `mini.pick` is configured. According to the documentation for [`mini.pick`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c404fc5717866ff738aadeeb1f54ab8ed270ae1e/doc/mini-pick.txt#L689-L780), you can **register** a custom function to handle buffers, as explained in [`registry`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c404fc5717866ff738aadeeb1f54ab8ed270ae1e/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1212-L1239).

Additionally, as mentioned in [`buffers`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c404fc5717866ff738aadeeb1f54ab8ed270ae1e/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1164-L1185), it's possible to **map** keys like `<C-d>` to perform specific actions on buffers, such as deleting them.

Thus, the code should be modified as follows to achieve the expected behavior:
<details><summary>Code (spoiler)</summary> 

```lua
local pick = require("mini.pick")
pick.registry.buffers = function(local_opts, opts)
    local_opts = local_opts or {}

    -- Delete the current buffer
    local wipeout_cur = function()
        vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(MiniPick.get_picker_matches().current.bufnr, {})
        MiniPick.builtin.buffers(local_opts, opts)
    end

    -- Map <C-d> to delete the buffer
    local buffer_mappings = { wipeout = { char = "<C-d>", func = wipeout_cur } }

    -- Show buffers with short names
    local show = function(buf_id, items, query)
        vim.tbl_map(function(i) i.text = vim.fn.fnamemodify(i.text, ":t") end, items)
        MiniPick.default_show(buf_id, items, query, { show_icons = true })
    end

    -- Merge options
    opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", {
        source = { show = show },
        mappings = buffer_mappings,
    }, opts or {})

    return MiniPick.builtin.buffers(local_opts, opts)
end
```
</details>

With this modification, the buffer will be deleted correctly when `<C-d>` is pressed, and the buffer list will be updated, showing only the short file names.

Yes, `<C-d>` is not an "out of the box" key to delete a buffer and requires custom configuration. This is [mentioned in the help](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c404fc5717866ff738aadeeb1f54ab8ed270ae1e/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1172-L1176).

Also, @Kogaraashi1, please use English to communicate here (auto-translation should be fine). This will help both people who try to answer questions and who will try to search information here in the future.

---

> According to the documentation for [`mini.pick`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c404fc5717866ff738aadeeb1f54ab8ed270ae1e/doc/mini-pick.txt#L689-L780), you can **register** a custom function to handle buffers, as explained in [`registry`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c404fc5717866ff738aadeeb1f54ab8ed270ae1e/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1212-L1239).

After reading it second time, this seems correct, but a bit confusing. A "custom function to handle buffers" is meant here as "custom function that starts a buffer picker", right? I initially thought that "handle buffers" meant as "delete the buffer".
